title: While Loops
objective: Control repetition using a condition that changes over time.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A while loop repeats a block of code for as long as its condition evaluates to True. Think of it as an if statement that checks again after the block finishes.

The key idea is changing state. Something inside the loop normally changes a variable, receives new input, or reaches an exit condition. If nothing can make the condition false, the program may run forever.
Use a while loop when you know the condition that should end the repetition, but you do not necessarily know in advance how many repetitions will occur.
explanation.rule: Use while when you know the condition that should stop the repetition, but not necessarily the number of repetitions.

examples.title: Countdown
examples.code:
count = 5

while count > 0:
    print(count)
    count -= 1

print("FORGE!")
examples.note: Each pass reduces count. Once it reaches 0, the condition is false and the loop ends.

checks.question: Why does a countdown loop eventually stop?
options: Python automatically limits while loops to five passes.
The counter changes until the loop condition becomes false.
The print function ends the loop.

feedback.correct: Correct — the changing counter eventually makes the condition false.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Look for the value that changes each pass.

assignment.title: Forge Countdown
assignment.brief: Write forge_countdown(start) using a while loop. Print every number from start to 1, then print FORGE!.
requirements: Do not use a for loop.
Print each number from start down to 1.
Print FORGE! after the loop ends.
assignment.starterCode:
def forge_countdown(start):
    # Write your while loop here.
    pass

forge_countdown(5)
assignment.solutionCode:
def forge_countdown(start):
    count = start
    while count > 0:
        print(count)
        count -= 1
    print("FORGE!")

forge_countdown(5)
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    forge_countdown(3)
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: What value should change on every pass through the loop?
Your condition can stay true while the counter is greater than zero.
Print the counter, then subtract one from it.
FORGE! belongs after the loop has finished.
